fleet.fence.confirm:
Turn on LAN isolation on "{name}"?

- The worker creates a Docker network (cashpilot-isolated) and one firewall table (ip cashpilot) on its host.
- Each running earner on Docker's default bridge is redeployed once onto that network. Storj gets its full clean stop first, so it can take a few minutes.
- Stopped earners stay stopped and move the next time you deploy them.
- Identities and data are kept: the same volumes and settings are used.

To undo it, set CASHPILOT_ISOLATION=off on the worker and redeploy the earners.

While it is missing, earners on its network can reach this host's own services, and they may still reach the internet if another masquerade rule on the host covers them. Deploys are refused until it is back. To run without the fence, set CASHPILOT_ISOLATION=off on the worker.

preflight.gpu_check_yourself: This needs a supported GPU passed through to the container. Without one it will start and then sit idle, earning nothing.
preflight.machine_has_nvidia_gpu_reaches: This machine has an NVIDIA GPU. {name} reaches it only through the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, which CashPilot cannot see from here. If it is not installed, install it ({toolkit_url}) and run `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker && sudo systemctl restart docker` before you deploy.
preflight.machine_identifies_itself_host: This machine identifies itself as a hosted/VPS server, and this service requires a residential IP. Datacentre addresses are usually detected and rejected — expect little or nothing, and possibly a banned account.
preflight.machine_publishes_no_build_onl: This machine is {fam} ({machine}) and {name} publishes no build for it, only {have}. The container will not start: Docker pulls the wrong build and it dies with 'exec format error'. The one exception is a Docker that runs foreign images under emulation (Docker Desktop with Rosetta, or binfmt/qemu), which CashPilot cannot check.
preflight.needs_least_disk_you_can: Needs at least {min_storage} of disk you can commit for months. Storage payouts accrue slowly and part of the balance is held back and forfeited if the node is abandoned early — running one for a month is worse than not running it at all.
preflight.needs_residential_ip_vps_datac: This needs a residential IP. On a VPS or datacentre connection it typically earns far less, or the account is banned outright. CashPilot cannot check your connection type, so this one is on you.
preflight.nothing_stands_out_should_work: Nothing stands out — {name} should work normally here.
preflight.provider_forbids_running_softw: This provider forbids running its software in Docker containers, on virtual machines, on home servers, or for monetisation — which is exactly what CashPilot does. Their stated penalty is termination without notice and cancellation of any pending payment. Deploying this here means accepting that risk knowingly.
preflight.shares_gpu_already_running_mac: {name} shares the GPU with {sharing}, already running on this machine. Expect each to earn less than it would alone.
preflight.should_work_provided_points_be: {name} should work, provided the points below are true of your setup.
preflight.wants_least_below_still_runs: Wants at least {min_bandwidth}. Below that it still runs, it just earns proportionally less. CashPilot does not measure your connection.
preflight.will_most_likely_earn_nothing: {name} will most likely earn nothing here. You can deploy it anyway.
preflight.will_probably_earn_less_here: {name} will probably earn less here than the catalog range suggests.
settings.about.desc_html: CashPilot checks GitHub for the latest release. Update runs the documented docker compose pull && docker compose up -d for you, from a one-shot helper container — it installs the newest patch of the image series your compose file pins. Moving to a newer series still means editing the image tags: read UPGRADING.md first, then update the UI host first and every worker after it. Installs not managed by Compose get the manual commands instead.
settings.about.title: About and updates
settings.collection.desc: Credentials for automated earnings tracking. Only services with a built-in collector are shown. You don't need to deploy containers through CashPilot — just add your credentials.
settings.collection.title: Earnings collection
settings.env.desc_html: These are read from the environment when CashPilot starts. Variables set via Docker -e flags are shown locked; the rest can be stored here, but a stored value does not take effect — set it in your compose file or Unraid template and restart. Several of them cannot change at runtime at all: the session key signs logins already in use, the data directory is where the open database lives, and the fleet key is what enrolled workers already hold.

settings.health.desc: How old each stored credential is, and when it is expected to stop working. Credential values are never shown here — only which one it is and how it is doing.
settings.health.title: Credential health
settings.identities.desc: The device names and ids CashPilot deployed each service with, per box. They stay here after you remove a service, so you can find the device at the provider or give a new box the same id. Each value is hidden until you show or copy it, and every show is written to the audit log. Passwords, keys and wallet seeds are never kept here. You can change the id a box runs, add an id CashPilot did not deploy with, and download the whole list after you enter your password.
settings.identities.title: Device ids
settings.restore.desc_html: Put a node identity or wallet back from a .cpbackup file made with a passphrase: Mysterium, ProxyBase or Anyone. The restore only creates a new container on a box that does not run the service, and never writes over a running one. To replace a running identity, download its backup first, then remove the service from that box on the dashboard and say yes when it asks to delete its data. Then restore here. Files sealed to a key, Storj and Sia use the command line steps.
